title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pages 774–777 of the 'suite' to La Longue Marche): x is a puncture or boundary point of a surface. S_x is the circle of directions at x (the boundary circle of the real oriented blow-up). D_x^* is a small punctured disc around x. Grothendieck wants a canonical equivalence Θ: Π_1(S_x) → Revêtements(D_x^*) (81). Through it, the isomorphisms between 'tangential' fibre functors γ, γ' become path classes in the circle of directions (80). He does not want to define (80) by hand. He wants a base-point-free, combinatorial description of Π_1(S_x), and uses the poset A_x of arcs of S_x. These are the closed connected proper subsets, i.e. arcs, and on this page point-subsets are clearly included among them. The ordered category A_x has inclusions as arrows, and Gr(A_x) is its enveloping groupoid, i.e. the localization inverting all arrows. The previous page asserts that Gr(A_x) ≃ Π_1(S_x).

This page makes the claim precise. Let Gr_0(A_x) be the full subgroupoid of Gr(A_x) on the singleton subsets {a}. There is a canonical equivalence Gr_0(A_x) ≃ Π_1(S_x) (83):
- On objects it is {a} ↦ a.
- For an arc A with endpoints a, b, the inclusions {a} ⊂ A ⊃ {b} become invertible in Gr. Their composite gives an arrow {a} → {b} (84).
- This arrow is sent to the homotopy class of the path running along A from a to b.

Consequence (85)/(86): for any groupoid G, functors Π_1(S_x) → G are the same as functors A_x → G, since any functor from the poset to a groupoid factors uniquely through the localization. The next page gives the criterion for such a Ψ to be an equivalence:
- G is connected with vertex groups ≅ Z.
- The loop {a} → A ← {b} → B ← {a}, for the two complementary arcs A, B with endpoints a ≠ b, maps to a generator of Aut(Ψ{a}).

The plan is then to build Θ as a functor from the poset of arcs to coverings of D_x^*, sending an arc (a sector of directions) to a simply connected covering space over D_x^*.

This is a standard topological lemma: the fundamental groupoid of the circle is presented as the localization of a poset of contractible pieces. It serves to make the 'circle of tangential base points' picture canonical and base-point free.
errors: Minor inconsistency: (82) seems to exclude singletons ('non réduits à des pts', possibly a deleted phrase), yet (83) uses the full subcategory on singleton subsets. The construction needs singletons to be objects of A_x.

The statement Gr(A_x) ≃ Π_1(S_x) is asserted ('on sait') without proof. It follows from a nerve/Quillen-type argument (the nerve of the poset of proper arcs, points included, is homotopy equivalent to S^1) or from van Kampen. It is correct, but nontrivial with closed arcs, because two arcs can have a disconnected intersection.

In the criterion on the next page, a ≠ b is needed so that the two complementary arcs A, B are defined. With that, the criterion is correct: connected plus image of the generator of π_1 being a generator gives full faithfulness and essential surjectivity.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid of S^1 as the localization (enveloping groupoid) of the poset of arcs, restricted to point-objects
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid as localization of a poset of contractible opens/closeds (Quillen/McCord/Segal nerve theorem; Thomason-style categorical models of homotopy types)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Segal 1968, McCord 1966, Quillen 1973 (Theorem A); Gabriel–Zisman 1967 for localization
ideas.where_published: Spirit appears in Pursuing Stacks (categories as models of homotopy types); this specific arc-poset lemma likely appears only in the Longue Marche manuscripts

ideas.what: Functors Π_1(S_x) → G are the same as functors from the arc poset to G, with a criterion for being an equivalence (connected, π_1 = Z, loop maps to a generator)
ideas.modern_name: Universal property of localization / local systems on S^1 as functors on a poset of arcs (constructible/cosheaf description)

ideas.what: Canonical equivalence between Π_1 of the circle of directions S_x and the category of universal coverings of the punctured disc D_x^* (tangential base points parametrized by directions)
ideas.modern_name: Tangential base points / real oriented blow-up boundary circle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (Le groupe fondamental de la droite projective moins trois points); Ihara; Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Longue Marche (1981) discusses base points at infinity and tangential directions in the Teichmüller tower context

deep.surprise_reason: A careful, base-point-free combinatorial presentation of Π_1(S^1) via the poset of arcs. It serves a construction of tangential base points as directions at a puncture. Mathematically standard; at most a historical detail of how Grothendieck set up tangential base points before Deligne's published treatment.
transcription_corrections: 'donc l'un des objets est A_x' should read 'dont l'un des objets ...' — more precisely, 'dont les objets sont les sous-ensembles ponctuels'.
'et soit . alors une équivalence canonique' likely reads 'on a alors une équivalence canonique'.
'pour tout arc [-?-] A' — the struck-out symbol before A is a false start; read 'pour tout arc A d'extrémités a, b'.
In (84) the arrows are {a} → A ← {b} (inclusions of singletons), giving {a} ≃ {b} in Gr(A_x).
Header '776' is the page number (manuscript p. 776); 'Gr_0(A_x)' is a marginal title.
Next page: 'S_n', 'A_n', 'D_n^*' should be S_x, A_x, D_x^*.
